james: Quick Q — implementing client retries for chunked upload / streaming endpoints that are non-idempotent. If we get 429 or 5xx, should SDK auto-retry by default? Do we prefer returning error and asking caller to retry with idempotency-key? cc @emily @linh

emily: Short answer: don't blindly auto-retry non-idempotent uploads. If we can't make the operation idempotent, surface the failure to the app. For 429 -> follow Retry-After if present; for 5xx -> can retry with backoff but only when we can guarantee no double-commit.

linh: Checklist for SDKs:
- require or optionally accept "Idempotency-Key" header (uuid v4)
- for chunked/streaming, add "Session-Id" + "Chunk-Index" so server can dedupe
- honor Retry-After on 429
- exponential backoff + full jitter for 5xx: recommend base=200ms, cap=10s, max_attempts=6

Example suggested backoff (pseudo):
```
base = 200ms
attempt = 0
while attempt < max_attempts:
  wait = random(0, base * 2 ** attempt)
  sleep(wait)
  attempt += 1
```

casey: For streaming uploads we implemented a resume token: after first ack server returns "Resume-Token". On reconnect clients send Resume-Token + next chunk index. Also keep commit separate: commit() is idempotent if called with Idempotency-Key.

rk: Edge cases to test: network drop after server accepted chunks but before commit -> client should retry commit with same Idempotency-Key. Also don't retry on 4xx except 429.

devex-bot: created issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/451 for SDK docs + example code :sparkles:

james: Great, I'll add Idempotency-Key to the JS and Python clients and wire up Retry-After handling. Will ping when PR is ready, thanks!
